notes:
Top-line: Enterprise buyer, heavy security/procurement constraints. Want Redwood Dedicated with VPC + on-prem option for EU/US data residency.

Key technical ask: guaranteed throughput + latency SLOs tied to reserved GPU commit.
 - Target SLOs: p95 latency <120ms for chat at expected concurrency (200 concurrent sessions), p95 latency <60ms for embeddings when routed to dedicated pool.
 - Throughput: baseline reserved capacity to sustain 75k tokens/min; burst plan up to 150k tokens/min for 30 mins/day.
 - Reserved GPU planning: proposing 8x A100-equivalent baseline with autoscale policy that allows 2x burst. Need clear billing for burst minutes vs reserved.
 - Fall-back/failover: require automated fallback to compatible model variant in different region; but for regulated data region failover must remain within data residency constraints.

Procurement/security blockers (primary):
 - DPA/MSA redlines: Legal insists on lowering Redwood liability cap to at least equal to fees paid in 12 months; wants EU-style data processing clauses and stronger data residency guarantees.
 - SLA negotiation: Palisade requires uptime SLAs with financial penalties that scale (not just service credits), and termination rights if SLO misses exceed 3x in a rolling 90-day period. Redwood default credits insufficient.
 - Insurance: Procurement requires cyber liability policy proof — minimum $5M coverage and vendor-level certificate. Broker needs language for indemnity tied to subcontractors.
 - Audit & compliance: Request for right-to-audit, on-site audits for Dedicated nodes, and annual pen-tests report. SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence must be provided.
 - Background checks: For any engineers with access to customer-dedicated infra, Palisade asks for background-check attestation and tight IAM controls.

Quotes / call snippets: "We can tolerate limited credits, but we need real penalties tied to missed throughput guarantees — otherwise procurement won't sign." — Head of Procurement.
"If the MSA indemnity doesn't move, our risk committee will block the deal." — GC.

Operational asks / POC success criteria:
 - Perf: p95 latency targets met for 14 consecutive days under production-correlated load.
 - Capacity: sustained tokens/min targets met and autoscale/burst behavior validated in failover scenario.
 - Evidence: SOC2 Type II report + ISO certificate + sample cert of cyber insurance.
 - Contract: MSA/DPA redlines agreed or an escalation path to exec legal; addendum for SLA financials if needed.

Next steps (short):
 - Redwood legal to provide sample MSA with suggested concessions (liability cap, more granular SLA credits, audit language) — due 2026-03-08.
 - Procurement to request vendor cyber insurance cert from Redwood — target 2026-03-10.
 - SE to run focused perf tuning (quantization, batching, kernel parameters) to hit p95 targets — perf report due 2026-03-05.
 - Schedule executive procurement review (Palisade GC + CFO + Redwood AE/Legal) week of 2026-03-15.
